_comment: Least-privilege ECS TASK ROLE policy for the VM Pool Manager service (pool_manager/). This is the TASK role the pool-manager process assumes when hosted on ECS/Fargate — DISTINCT from (a) the MicroVM EXECUTION role (MicroVMSandboxExecRole, iam/exec-role-permissions.json) that each spawned MicroVM runs under, and (b) the build role. Like iam/proxy-role-permissions.json, this file is DOCUMENTATION of the exact grant to attach when the service moves to a hosted role; setup_iam.sh does NOT apply it today because the pool manager currently runs locally under your own dev/admin AWS credentials. Current operating assumption: desiredCount=1 (one pool-manager instance). Permissions are derived 1:1 from the boto3 calls in pool_manager/aws_backend.py. ACTION-PREFIX CAVEAT: the boto3 client id is 'lambda-microvms'; the IAM action prefix is assumed to be 'lambda-microvms:' with PascalCase action names matching the API operations below, but this MUST be confirmed against the lambda-microvms service's IAM documentation — adjust the prefix/casing if the service publishes a different IAM namespace. No actions were invented: the seven control-plane actions map exactly to run_microvm, get_microvm, list_microvms, suspend_microvm, resume_microvm, terminate_microvm, create_microvm_auth_token.

Statement._comment: run_microvm is called with executionRoleArn=self.exec_role_arn (pool_manager/aws_backend.py:168), so the task must be allowed to PassRole the MicroVM execution role (EXEC_ROLE_NAME=MicroVMSandboxExecRole in scripts/config.sh). Scoped to that one role, and conditioned on the role only being passed to the lambda-microvms service.

Only needed when the Aurora read-write DB password (feeding STORAGE_CONNECTION for the shared pool_vms ledger under STORAGE_BACKEND=postgres) is resolved from Secrets Manager. Scoped to the read-write DB secret pattern (AURORA_RW_SECRET_NAME=microvm/proxy-db/readwrite in scripts/config.sh). Remove this statement if the connection string / password is injected another way.
